title: Why the derivative of x² is 2x

beats.narration: Here is a question that the derivative formula hides. At a single point, a curve has no width, so what could its slope possibly mean?
beats.title: Why the derivative of x² is 2x
beats.subtitle: A limit you can see
beats.notes: Open with the conceptual tension, not the formula.

beats.narration: The answer is a process. Start with an average slope over an interval, then shrink the interval toward a single point.
beats.heading: The question
beats.notes: Set up the two quantities the episode will connect.

beats.narration: For a straight line, slope is rise over run. For a parabola, the slope changes at every point. So we need a slope that belongs to one point, not to an interval.
beats.heading: What we already know
items: A line has one slope: rise over run.
A parabola changes steepness at every point.
An interval has an average slope; a point needs a limit.
beats.notes: Bridge from prior knowledge to the need for a limit.

beats.narration: Take x squared and two inputs, one and three. The secant line through those points has slope four. That is the average rate over the interval.
beats.speech: Take x squared and two inputs, one and three. The secant line through those points has slope four. That is the average rate over the interval.
beats.heading: Average slope on [1, 3]
beats.notes: This graph shows that the secant slope is an average rate because it uses two distinct inputs.

beats.narration: Now move the second point closer: from three to two. The average slope drops to three. The interval is smaller, and the average is closer to what we want.
beats.heading: Shrink the interval
beats.notes: This graph shows the average slope changing as the interval shrinks; it motivates the limit.

beats.narration: Keep shrinking h. The average slopes are four, three, two point five, two point one. They are converging to two, but no single average is the answer.
beats.heading: A sequence of averages
beats.notes: Make the numerical pattern explicit before the visual limit.

beats.narration: Watch the secant line as h goes to zero. The line pivots toward the tangent, and the average slope approaches two. That limiting line is the derivative at x equals one.
beats.heading: The secant becomes the tangent
beats.notes: This graph shows the crux visually: the secant line's limiting position is the tangent, and its slope is the derivative.

beats.narration: Formally, the derivative is the limit of the difference quotient as h approaches zero. The quotient is an average slope; the limit is the instantaneous slope.
beats.speech: Formally, the derivative is the limit of the difference quotient as h approaches zero. The quotient is an average slope; the limit is the instantaneous slope.
beats.heading: The definition
beats.notes: The formal bridge from geometry to algebra.

beats.narration: For f of x equals x squared, the numerator becomes x plus h squared minus x squared. Expanding gives two x h plus h squared.
beats.speech: For f of x equals x squared, the numerator becomes x plus h, squared, minus x squared. Expanding gives two x h plus h squared.
beats.heading: Substitute and expand
beats.notes: Keep the h in the denominator visible: the cancellation is the next beat.

beats.narration: Dividing by h is allowed because h is not zero during the limit. The quotient simplifies to two x plus h. Then the limit is two x.
beats.speech: Dividing by h is allowed because h is not zero during the limit. The quotient simplifies to two x plus h. Then the limit is two x.
beats.heading: Cancel, then take the limit
beats.notes: The crux: cancellation is valid before the limit because h is nonzero on a punctured neighborhood.

beats.narration: At x equals one, the formula gives a slope of two. The tangent line is y equals two x minus one, and it touches the parabola at one, one.
beats.heading: The tangent at x = 1
beats.notes: This graph shows the formula as a geometric object: the tangent line at (1,1) has slope 2.

beats.narration: The common mistake is to set h equal to zero too early. That gives zero over zero. The correct move is to cancel h first, then let h approach zero.
beats.heading: The trap

beats.narration: This is why the cancellation step is the crux. It removes the thing that would make the denominator zero, and it leaves a finite expression whose limit we can read.
beats.heading: Why cancellation matters
items: The limit never evaluates the quotient at h = 0.
Cancellation is valid for every h ≠ 0.
The simplified expression has a finite limit.
beats.notes: Make the logical status of the cancellation explicit.

beats.narration: The derivative is also a function. For x squared, f prime of x equals two x. At each x, the height of the line gives the slope of the parabola.
beats.heading: The derivative as a function
beats.notes: This graph shows the derivative as a new function: its height at x is the slope of x² at x.

beats.narration: So the derivative is not a formula to memorize. It is the limit of an average slope, and the algebra is what survives the limit.
beats.heading: What we established
items: A secant slope is an average rate over an interval.
The limit turns that average into an instantaneous rate.
Cancelling h is the step that makes the limit finite.
